title: The Hunt for Red Dual AGNs I: Spatially-Resolved Mid-IR Dual AGNs in the DeCam Legacy Survey
comment: 35 pages, including 5 tables, 10 figures, and 4 appendix sections. Submitted to ApJ; feedback welcome!
summary: Theoretical studies predict that dual AGNs are a critical stage of galaxy merger-driven supermassive black hole growth. Systematic searches for dual AGNs typically target late-stage mergers ($\leq10$ kpc nuclear separations) and select AGNs based on optical diagnostics. Yet, simulations predict that obscuration can occur early in the merger sequence, and that a significant fraction of dual AGNs can be found beyond $10$ kpc. Here, we report on a new sample of 157 spatially resolved mid-IR dual AGNs candidates selected based upon their mid-IR $W1-W2$ colors from the Wide-Field Infrared Survey Explorer and optically classified as galaxy merger candidates using imaging from the Dark Energy Camera Legacy Survey. Spectroscopic results are presented for approximately 2/3 of the sample. 76 candidates have been confirmed to reside in galaxy mergers; among these, 13 have been confirmed as bona fide mid-IR dual AGNs, while 63 represent strong dual AGN candidates that require further examination. 46 candidates have been rejected as non-merger contaminants (foreground-background AGNs, separations inconsistent with interacting galaxies, etc.). 35 candidates still await spectroscopic coverage. The confirmed and high confidence dual AGN candidates exhibit separations of 14.5-129 kpc; $>50$% reside at separations $>50$ kpc. Confirmed and high confidence candidates also exhibit a diversity of nuclear optical BPT classes. Seyfert-Seyferts and Seyfert-HIIs dominate the overall BPT pairs sample. 31% of confirmed mid-IR dual AGNs reside in multi-mergers involving three or more galaxies. The diversity in AGN properties and environments identified in this work highlights the importance of multiwavelength selection strategies and analyses in the quest to holistically understand dual AGNs as a population.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a sample of 157 spatially resolved mid-IR dual AGN candidates selected via WISE W1-W2 colors and DECaLS optical imaging. Of ~2/3 spectroscopically observed, 13 are confirmed dual AGNs, 63 are strong candidates, and 46 are rejected. Confirmed/high-confidence candidates span separations of 14.5–129 kpc, with >50% beyond 50 kpc, including multi-merger systems (31%). The results underscore the need for multiwavelength strategies to capture the full dual AGN population.
AI.motivation: Theoretical studies predict dual AGNs as a critical phase in merger-driven supermassive black hole growth, but systematic searches often focus on late-stage mergers (≤10 kpc) using optical diagnostics, potentially missing obscured and wide-separation dual AGNs that simulations indicate appear earlier in the merger sequence.
AI.method: Mid-IR dual AGN candidates were selected using WISE W1-W2 colors, spatially resolved at separations >10 kpc, and optically classified as galaxy merger candidates from DECaLS imaging. Spectroscopic follow-up (~2/3 of the sample) was used to confirm/reject candidates via BPT classification and redshift consistency.
AI.result: 76 candidates confirmed as mergers; 13 as bona fide dual AGNs, 63 as strong candidates. 46 rejected as non-merger contaminants. 35 still awaiting spectroscopy. Confirmed/high-confidence candidates have separations 14.5–129 kpc (>50% >50 kpc). Diverse BPT classes found; Seyfert-Seyfert and Seyfert-HII pairs dominate. 31% of confirmed dual AGNs reside in multi-mergers (≥3 galaxies).
AI.conclusion: Wide-separation dual AGNs (>10 kpc, often >50 kpc) are common and can be identified via mid-IR selection combined with optical merger morphology. The diversity in nuclear types and environments highlights that multiwavelength selection is essential for a holistic understanding of the dual AGN population.

title: Massive Galaxies Form Early and Gray: Stellar Assembly and Dust Attenuation at $\mathbf{z>3.5}$ from CAPERS
comment: 24 pages, 11 figures, submitted to ApJL
summary: The stellar mass assembly of massive galaxies in the first few billion years of cosmic history remains a central challenge in galaxy formation. Galaxies with $M_\star \gtrsim 10^{10}M_\odot$ observed at $z \gtrsim 4$ must grow rapidly under conditions of intense gas accretion, feedback, and dust production. Observationally, their star-formation histories (SFHs) have been poorly constrained due to degeneracies inherent to broadband photometry. The advent of JWST enables direct spectroscopic access to detailed continuum shapes and rest-frame optical diagnostics at high redshift, providing a critical opportunity to reconstruct formation timescales of massive early galaxies. Here, we investigate massive galaxies using joint spectro-photometric SED fitting of JWST/NIRSpec prism spectroscopy from the CANDELS-Area Prism Epoch of Reionization Survey (CAPERS). Our sample comprises 148 galaxies selected photometrically with log $(M_\star/M_\odot) > 9.5$ at $z > 3.5$. We find that the most massive galaxies (log $(M_\star/M_\odot) > 10.5$) preferentially exhibit shallow, gray dust attenuation curves, consistent with higher dust optical depths and large grain sizes. We also find significant diversity in the time at which galaxies form 25% of their stellar mass. While formation timescales converge toward later cosmic times, galaxies with lower sSFR ($\lesssim -9$) at the observation epoch formed significantly earlier than systems with higher sSFRs. Across the full mass range, inferred assembly times are systematically earlier than model predictions, suggesting more rapid early growth than currently captured theoretically. These results underscore the importance of spectroscopic constraints and flexible SFH and dust models for reconstructing high-redshift massive galaxy formation histories.

AI.tldr: Using JWST/NIRSpec prism spectroscopy on 148 massive galaxies at z>3.5, this study finds that the most massive galaxies exhibit shallow gray dust attenuation, diverse formation timescales, and systematically earlier assembly than model predictions, highlighting the need for spectroscopic constraints and flexible SFH/dust models.
AI.motivation: The stellar mass assembly of massive galaxies in the early universe (z≳4) remains poorly understood due to degeneracies in broadband photometry, and their star-formation histories have been difficult to constrain observationally.
AI.method: Joint spectro-photometric SED fitting of JWST/NIRSpec prism spectroscopy from the CAPERS survey on 148 galaxies with log(M*/M⊙)>9.5 at z>3.5.
AI.result: (1) Most massive galaxies (log(M*/M⊙)>10.5) show shallow gray dust attenuation curves; (2) significant diversity in the epoch of 25% mass formation; (3) lower sSFR galaxies formed earlier; (4) inferred assembly times are systematically earlier than model predictions across the full mass range.
AI.conclusion: Spectroscopic constraints from JWST, together with flexible SFH and dust models, are essential for reconstructing high-redshift massive galaxy formation histories, which appear more rapid than current theoretical models capture.

title: When galaxies burst: enhanced shot-noise for line-intensity mapping in the JWST era
comment: 6 pages, 5 figures (with appendices: 11 pages, 7 figures)
summary: Recent JWST observations indicate that star formation at $z\!\sim\!4-6$ is more stochastic than previously assumed, with rms log-SFR scatter $\sim\!0.6$ dex at $M_h\!\sim\!10^{11}M_{\odot}$, growing toward smaller halos and time-correlated on $\sim\!25$ Myr. This is significantly higher than the typical $\sim\!0.3$ dex phenomenological lognormal scatter assumed in standard line-intensity mapping (LIM) forecasts. We propagate the JWST-era burstiness through to the LIM shot-noise power spectrum and show that the result is a simple multiplicative correction: the deterministic shot noise multiplied by a line-dependent boost factor $B_λ$ derived in closed form by convolving the SFR correlation function with the stellar-population-synthesis kernel of each line. At $z\!\sim\!6$, we find $B_{{\rm H}α}\!\simeq\!7$ and $B\!\sim\!2.5$-$3.5$ for longer-window tracers ([CII], CO, UV) - factors of $\sim\!2$-$5$ above the standard prescription, and growing further toward higher redshift. The enhancement transforms the LIM landscape: it improves auto-spectrum detectability and suppresses lower-redshift interloper contamination, but degrades cosmological applications such as BAO that rely on a clean clustering measurement. Crucially, it also opens a new use of LIM as a diagnostic of high-redshift star-formation physics beyond the regime of individually resolved galaxies: redshift tomography of a single line constrains the amplitude and mass dependence of the burstiness, while cross-line shot-noise correlations probe its time coherence.

AI.tldr: JWST reveals that star formation at z~4-6 is more bursty (scatter ~0.6 dex) than assumed (~0.3 dex) in standard LIM forecasts. This burstiness boosts LIM shot noise by factors of ~2-7 depending on the line, improving detectability but degrading cosmological applications, and enabling new diagnostics of high-redshift star-formation physics.
AI.motivation: Recent JWST observations show star formation at z~4-6 is more stochastic than the typical ~0.3 dex lognormal scatter assumed in standard line-intensity mapping (LIM) forecasts. It's unclear how this burstiness propagates into LIM power spectrum predictions and affects observational strategies.
AI.method: The authors derive a closed-form multiplicative correction to the deterministic shot noise: a line-dependent boost factor B_λ obtained by convolving the SFR correlation function with the stellar-population-synthesis kernel of each emission line. They apply this to Hα, [CII], CO, and UV tracers at z~6.
AI.result: At z~6, B_Hα ≈ 7, B ~ 2.5-3.5 for longer-window tracers ([CII], CO, UV), representing factors of ~2-5 above standard prescriptions, growing further toward higher redshift. The enhancement improves auto-spectrum detectability and suppresses interloper contamination but degrades BAO and other clustering-based cosmological applications.
AI.conclusion: JWST-era burstiness transforms the LIM landscape. It enables new diagnostics: redshift tomography of a single line constrains burstiness amplitude and mass dependence, while cross-line shot-noise correlations probe its time coherence, opening LIM as a tool for high-redshift star-formation physics beyond individual galaxy resolution.

title: Determining star formation histories and age-metallicity relations with convolutional neural networks
summary:
We aim to develop a state-of-the-art tool to infer detailed star formation histories (SFHs) and age-metallicity relations from realistic observational data, while mitigating classical degeneracies and substantially reducing computational cost. In particular, we seek to exploit the complementarity of spectroscopic and photometric data to improve constraints on the spatially resolved SFH and metallicity evolution of nearby galaxies in the PHANGS collaboration.
  We construct and train a convolutional neural network (CNN) that combines convolutional layers, attention mechanisms, and a shared latent space to jointly predict SFHs and metallicities in 16 age bins. The network simultaneously processes integral-field spectroscopic data from PHANGS-MUSE and five-band photometric fluxes from PHANGS-HST. Training is performed on a dataset of 165\,000 synthetic spectra and photometric measurements spanning a broad range of SFH shapes, metallicity evolution, dust attenuation, and signal-to-noise ratios representative of the observations.
  The CNN accurately recovers SFHs and age-metallicity relations over a wide range of evolutionary scenarios. The inferred luminosity- and mass-weighted mean ages and metallicities show negligible bias, with dispersions of $\sim0.12$ dex in age and $\sim0.03$ dex in metallicity. When applied to real PHANGS-MUSE and PHANGS-HST data for NGC\,3627, the network produces smooth, spatially coherent maps of stellar age and metallicity that recover physically meaningful structures, including younger populations tracing the spiral arms and star-forming regions. The CNN is approximately $5\times10^{3}$--$2\times10^{4}$ times faster than traditional full spectral fitting codes, providing a powerful and efficient alternative for the analysis of large spectro-photometric surveys.

AI.tldr: A CNN combining spectroscopy (MUSE) and photometry (HST) jointly infers spatially resolved star formation histories and age-metallicity relations for nearby galaxies, achieving ~0.12 dex age and ~0.03 dex metallicity precision while being 10³–10⁴× faster than traditional full spectral fitting.
AI.motivation: To develop a state-of-the-art tool that infers detailed SFHs and age-metallicity relations from realistic observational data while mitigating classical degeneracies, reducing computational cost, and exploiting the complementarity of spectroscopic and photometric data for spatially resolved studies of nearby galaxies in the PHANGS collaboration.
AI.method: A convolutional neural network combining convolutional layers, attention mechanisms, and a shared latent space to jointly predict SFHs and metallicities in 16 age bins from integral-field spectroscopic data (PHANGS-MUSE) and five-band HST photometry; trained on 165,000 synthetic spectra+photometry spanning a broad range of SFH shapes, metallicity evolution, dust attenuation, and SNR levels.
AI.result: Accurate recovery of SFHs and age-metallicity relations across diverse evolutionary scenarios; luminosity- and mass-weighted mean ages and metallicities show negligible bias with dispersions of ~0.12 dex in age and ~0.03 dex in metallicity; application to NGC 3627 yields smooth, spatially coherent stellar age and metallicity maps tracing spiral arms and star-forming regions; computational speedup of ~5×10³–2×10⁴× over traditional full spectral fitting.
AI.conclusion: The CNN provides a powerful, efficient alternative for analyzing large spectro-photometric surveys, enabling high-precision, spatially resolved SFH and metallicity inference at dramatically reduced computational cost.

title: Analysis of DQZ White Dwarf Evolution through Procyon
summary: Procyon is a great system to probe stellar evolution of non-interacting binaries. We present an extensive grid of MESA (Modules for Experiments in Stellar Astrophysics) evolutionary tracks to constrain the evolution of Procyon A and B. We systematically vary the initial parameters of our grid anchored by precise dynamical masses and spectroscopic determinations of effective temperature (T$_{eff}$) and luminosity ($L$) to match the stars' positions on the H-R Diagram. Our goal is two-fold: (i) to quantify how the inferred system age and the progenitor mass of Procyon B depend on metallicity ($Z$), mixing length ($α$), and core overshoot ($β$), and (ii) to determine the best fitting model of Procyon B within a model-based initial-to-final mass relationship (IMFR) for hydrogen-deficient white dwarfs. Our best-fit models reproduce the observed properties for both components, yielding $M_\mathrm{A}=1.487 \pm 0.095$ M$_{\odot}$, $M_\mathrm{B}=0.592\pm 0.082$ M$_{\odot}$, a system age of $2.23 \pm 0.90$ Gyr, and a white dwarf cooling age of $1.20\pm0.49$ Gyr for Procyon B, consistent with independent determinations. Our results point to higher core overshoot than the standard adopted range, with the best fits ranging from $β=0.5-1.0$. From our model grid, we map Procyon B to the initial-to-final mass relationship for H-deficient white dwarfs in the $1.9\!-\!2.6$ M$_{\odot}$ progenitor range. Additionally, we implement the accretion of heavy metals onto the surface of the WD and fit our isotopic abundances to spectroscopic observations. We outline the physics used in our analysis.

AI.tldr: The paper presents MESA evolutionary models to constrain the evolution of the Procyon binary system, finding best-fit masses, ages, and core overshoot parameters, and mapping Procyon B to the initial-to-final mass relationship for H-deficient white dwarfs.
AI.motivation: To use the Procyon non-interacting binary system as a probe of stellar evolution by constraining system parameters (age, progenitor mass) through precise dynamical masses and spectroscopic data, and to quantify how metallicity, mixing length, and core overshoot affect the inferred system properties.
AI.method: An extensive grid of MESA evolutionary tracks was constructed, systematically varying initial parameters (metallicity Z, mixing length α, core overshoot β) anchored by precise dynamical masses and spectroscopic Teff and luminosity measurements. Best-fitting models were identified by matching both stars' positions on the H-R Diagram, and heavy-metal accretion onto the WD surface was implemented to fit isotopic abundances to observations.
AI.result: Best-fit models yield MA = 1.487 ± 0.095 M⊙, MB = 0.592 ± 0.082 M⊙, system age = 2.23 ± 0.90 Gyr, and WD cooling age = 1.20 ± 0.49 Gyr for Procyon B. Higher core overshoot (β = 0.5–1.0) than standard range was found. Procyon B maps to the IMFR for H-deficient WDs in the 1.9–2.6 M⊙ progenitor range.
AI.conclusion: The results are consistent with independent determinations, demonstrating the utility of binary systems for constraining stellar evolution and white dwarf formation physics, with implications for core overshoot and the initial-to-final mass relationship.

title: Lyman-alpha Radiation Pressure in Dense Star Clusters: Implications for Star Formation and Winds at Cosmic Dawn
comment: 19 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to ApJ. Comments and suggestions welcome!
summary: Observations with the JWST in lensed fields have revealed that galaxies at cosmic dawn may concentrate their star formation in highly dense, compact, star clusters. The high columns and low metallicities encountered in their birth environments suggest that Lyman-alpha (Ly$α$) radiation pressure may be crucial to their formation and evolution. In this study, we address this question by post-processing snapshots from radiation hydrodynamic simulations of dense star cluster-forming clouds ($Σ_*\gtrsim10^3{M_\odot{pc}^{-2}}$) with a range of dust abundances ($Z_d=0-0.1Z_{d,\odot}$) using the COLT Monte Carlo code. We infer that Ly$α$ is likely to have mild (~10%) effects on the gas-to-star conversion efficiencies ($ε_*\gtrsim60$%) for $Z_d\gtrsim0.01Z_{d,\odot}$, and even in dust-free environments, $ε_*\gtrsim25$% - much higher than the <10% values typical of star-forming regions in the local Universe. This is because the densest filaments dominating stellar mass assembly ($n\gtrsim10^4{cm}^{-3}$) remain sub-Eddington ($f_{Edd}<1$). On the other hand, the bulk of the gas volume ($n\lesssim10^3{cm}^{-3}$) has $f_{Edd}>1$, with noticeable fractions having $f_{Edd}\gtrsim10$, implying that Ly$α$ can launch dynamically significant winds from these systems rapidly ($\lesssim$4Myr), with possible implications for ionizing photon escape and galactic outflows. The Ly$α$ force multiplier $M_F$ is highly sensitive to $Z_d$, with $M_F\lesssim3$ ($\lesssim 500$) for $0.1Z_{d,\odot}$ (dust-free) environments respectively. Nevertheless, Ly$α$ dominates over UV and IR radiation pressure at all values of $Z_d\lesssim0.1Z_{d,\odot}$, by factors of ~3-500. Our results suggest that Ly$α$ radiation pressure reinforces the emerging picture of locally efficient, bursty star formation accompanied by rapid outflows in galaxies at cosmic dawn.

AI.tldr: This study uses Monte Carlo radiative transfer simulations to show that Lyman-alpha radiation pressure has mild (~10%) effects on star formation efficiency in dense, compact star clusters at cosmic dawn (efficiencies remain ≥25% even in dust-free environments), but can drive rapid, dynamically significant winds from diffuse regions, with Lyα dominating over UV/IR radiation pressure by factors of 3–500 across sub-solar dust abundances.
AI.motivation: JWST observations reveal that galaxies at cosmic dawn concentrate star formation in dense, compact star clusters with high columns and low metallicities, suggesting that Lyman-alpha radiation pressure may be crucial to their formation and evolution—a question that has not been systematically addressed.
AI.method: The authors post-process snapshots from radiation hydrodynamic simulations of dense star cluster-forming clouds (Σ* ≳ 10³ M⊙ pc⁻²) with dust abundances Zd = 0–0.1 Z⊙ using the COLT Monte Carlo radiative transfer code to quantify the effects of Lyα radiation pressure.
AI.result: Lyα has mild (~10%) effects on gas-to-star conversion efficiencies (ε* ≳ 60% for Zd ≳ 0.01 Z⊙; ε* ≳ 25% in dust-free cases). Dense filaments (n ≳ 10⁴ cm⁻³) remain sub-Eddington (fEdd < 1), while diffuse gas (n ≲ 10³ cm⁻³) has fEdd > 1, with fractions reaching fEdd ≳ 10, driving rapid winds (≲4 Myr). The Lyα force multiplier ranges from MF ≲ 3 (0.1 Z⊙) to ≲ 500 (dust-free). Lyα dominates over UV and IR radiation pressure by factors of ~3–500.
AI.conclusion: Lyα radiation pressure reinforces the emerging picture of locally efficient, bursty star formation accompanied by rapid outflows in galaxies at cosmic dawn, with implications for ionizing photon escape and galactic outflows.

title: Spectral Disentangling Reveals Deep CNO-cycle Exposure in ET Cru
comment: Accepted for publication in The Astronomical Journal. 22 pages, 14 Figures, and 6 tables
summary: Binary stars undergoing mass transfer provide unique laboratories for testing stellar evolution. Here, we present a comprehensive photometric and spectroscopic analysis of the semi-detached system ET Cru. Using spectral disentangling, we independently determined the effective temperatures and chemical abundances of both components with high precision, including nine elements (eleven species). We find masses of $13.41\,M_\odot$ and $6.00\,M_\odot$ for the primary and secondary, respectively, with uncertainties of only $\sim$1.3%. The radii are $5.58\,R_\odot$ and $5.68\,R_\odot$, measured to within 0.4% and 0.5%. Surface gravities are constrained to better than 1%, while effective temperatures are determined to within 3-5%. The secondary exhibits extreme chemical anomalies, with severe carbon depletion and nitrogen enrichment far exceeding those reported in classical Algol systems. Multi-wavelength spectral energy distribution modelling yields a distance of $\sim$2.5 kpc, inconsistent with the $Gaia$ DR3 parallax, suggesting systematic astrometric uncertainties in the parallax distance. Together, these results establish ET Cru as a benchmark Algol-type binary, revealing direct spectroscopic evidence of deep CNO-cycle exposure in the donor and confirming the primary star as a rejuvenated gainer. ET Cru thus provides a chemically and dynamically illustrative case for understanding advanced binary interactions and the late evolutionary stages of massive-star evolution.

AI.tldr: ET Cru is a semi-detached Algol-type binary system analyzed via photometric and spectroscopic methods. The primary (13.41 M☉) and secondary (6.00 M☉) have precise masses, radii, surface gravities, and temperatures. The secondary shows extreme carbon depletion and nitrogen enrichment from deep CNO-cycle exposure, while the primary is a rejuvenated gainer. Distance from SED (~2.5 kpc) conflicts with Gaia DR3 parallax, indicating systematic astrometric issues.
AI.motivation: Binary stars undergoing mass transfer offer unique laboratories for testing stellar evolution, and ET Cru provides a benchmark case for studying advanced binary interactions and late-stage massive-star evolution.
AI.method: Comprehensive photometric and spectroscopic analysis using spectral disentangling to independently determine effective temperatures and chemical abundances of both components, including nine elements (eleven species). Multi-wavelength SED modelling for distance estimation.
AI.result: Primary mass 13.41 M☉, secondary mass 6.00 M☉ (uncertainties ~1.3%); radii 5.58 R☉ and 5.68 R☉ (uncertainties 0.4-0.5%); surface gravities better than 1%; temperatures within 3-5%. Secondary shows extreme chemical anomalies (C depletion, N enrichment). Distance ~2.5 kpc inconsistent with Gaia DR3 parallax.
AI.conclusion: ET Cru is a benchmark Algol-type binary with direct spectroscopic evidence of deep CNO-cycle exposure in the donor, confirming the primary as a rejuvenated gainer. It serves as a chemically and dynamically illustrative case for understanding binary interactions and massive-star evolution.

title: Ionization Structure and Metal Enrichment of the Galactic Center Minispiral Observed with JWST
comment: Main text 13 pages, 10 figures, 5 Tables. Submitted to ApJ. Comments welcomed
summary: Sgr A* is the nearest quiescent supermassive black hole, and its proximity offers a unique opportunity to study its surrounding fuel supply. We leverage extensive spatial and spectroscopic information provided by the \jwst/MIRI MRS instrument to disentangle mid-infrared ionized gas structures in the central 0.1 parsec of the Galaxy. The Galactic Minispiral's Bar and Northern Arm are revealed by their distinct morphological and kinematic signatures. Several compact ($<1$\arcsec) gas structures including X7 also appear within $\sim 0.05$ parsec of Sgr A* in the plane of the sky, moving with blue-shifted radial velocities $\gtrsim 600$ km/s. Fine structure line measurements spanning ionization energies $\sim 7 - 55$ eV are used to constrain the incident radiation field, metal abundances (neon, argon, sulfur, nickel, and iron), and dust depletion/destruction for each identified gas structure. Overall, the Minispiral gas metallicity is $\sim 1-2.5~Z_\sun$, with a Wolf-Rayet star-driven ionizing radiation field, and significant nickel and iron dust destruction. Increased flux at energies $\gtrsim 41$ eV suggests that the compact gas structures experience an additional harder ionizing radiation source, which is most likely driven by localized fast radiative shocks from stellar winds, a hypothetical Sgr A* outflow, and/or interactions with the ambient medium.

AI.tldr: This study uses JWST/MIRI MRS observations to analyze mid-infrared ionized gas structures within 0.1 parsec of Sgr A*, revealing the Bar and Northern Arm of the Galactic Minispiral, compact blue-shifted gas structures near the black hole, and constraining metallicity (~1-2.5 Z☉), radiation fields (Wolf-Rayet star-driven), and dust destruction, with evidence for an additional harder ionizing source in compact structures likely from shocks or outflows.
AI.motivation: To leverage the spatial and spectroscopic capabilities of JWST/MIRI MRS to disentangle and characterize the ionized gas structures fueling the nearest quiescent supermassive black hole, Sgr A*, at an unprecedented resolution within the central 0.1 parsec.
AI.method: JWST/MIRI MRS integral field spectroscopy was used to obtain morphological and kinematic maps of ionized gas structures. Fine structure line measurements across ionization energies 7–55 eV were employed to model the incident radiation field, metal abundances (Ne, Ar, S, Ni, Fe), and dust depletion/destruction for each identified gas component.
AI.result: The Minispiral's Bar and Northern Arm show distinct morphological and kinematic signatures. Compact structures (including X7) within ~0.05 parsec of Sgr A* exhibit blue-shifted radial velocities ≥600 km/s. Minispiral metallicity is ~1-2.5 Z☉ with a Wolf-Rayet star-driven ionizing field and significant Ni and Fe dust destruction. Compact structures show increased flux at energies ≥41 eV, indicating a harder radiation source.
AI.conclusion: The Galactic Minispiral gas is metal-rich and ionized primarily by Wolf-Rayet stars with substantial dust destruction. The compact gas structures near Sgr A* require an additional harder ionizing source, likely from fast radiative shocks driven by stellar winds, a potential Sgr A* outflow, or interactions with the ambient medium.

title: Constraining the Galactic Center Dark Cluster with ELT/MICADO Observations
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A (aa59043-26)
summary: The Galactic Center hosts the densest known stellar environment in the Milky Way, dominated by the massive black hole Sgr A* and the surrounding nuclear star cluster. Theory predicts that this region should also contain a large population of stellar compact objects (SCOs) - black holes, neutron stars, and white dwarfs - forming a "dark cluster" whose distribution and properties remain observationally unconstrained. These unseen stellar remnants are central to questions of mass segregation, cluster dynamics, and the expected rate of extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) detectable by future gravitational-wave observatories including LISA. Current evidence for SCOs in the Galactic Center is indirect, relying on dynamical mass measurements, X-ray surveys, and a small number of transient sources. Direct detections remain elusive due to crowding, extinction, and the sensitivity limits of existing instruments. We explore how upcoming facilities, in particular the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) with its first-light imager MICADO, can fundamentally transform this field. MICADO's combination of deep photometry, high spatial resolution, and precise astrometry will enable systematic searches for SCO-star binaries via photometric variability and orbital astrometric signatures, as well as direct detection of isolated accreting black holes interacting with the gas-rich Galactic Center environment. We outline the observational pathways, technical challenges, and expected sensitivities, showing that ELT/MICADO observations can provide the first quantitative constraints on the dark cluster population. Establishing these constraints will be pivotal for understanding the dynamical evolution of the Galactic Center, the role of compact remnants in nuclear star clusters, and the astrophysical context of gravitational-wave sources in galactic nuclei.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses how the ELT/MICADO instrument will enable the first direct observational constraints on the elusive population of stellar compact objects (black holes, neutron stars, white dwarfs) in the Galactic Center, advancing our understanding of dynamics, mass segregation, and EMRI rates for LISA.
AI.motivation: The Galactic Center should host a large "dark cluster" of stellar compact objects (SCOs), but their distribution and properties remain observationally unconstrained due to crowding, extinction, and instrument sensitivity limits. Understanding this population is key for mass segregation, cluster dynamics, and predicting EMRI rates for LISA.
AI.method: Simulations and sensitivity forecasts for ELT/MICADO observations, targeting SCO-star binaries via photometric variability and orbital astrometric signatures, as well as direct detection of isolated accreting black holes interacting with the gas-rich environment.
AI.result: ELT/MICADO observations can provide the first quantitative constraints on the dark cluster population, enabling systematic searches for SCO-star binaries and isolated accreting black holes.
AI.conclusion: Establishing constraints on the dark cluster will be pivotal for understanding Galactic Center dynamics, the role of compact remnants in nuclear star clusters, and the astrophysical context of gravitational-wave sources in galactic nuclei.

title: Direct Evidence of Non-Ideal Dissipative Dynamics in Solar Wind Magnetic Switchbacks
comment: 7 pages, 6 figures
summary: Magnetic switchbacks, large-amplitude, localized Alfvenic like rotations of the solar wind magnetic field, have been the subject of intensive investigation, with approximately 200 refereed papers published in the last decade. Yet, fundamental controversies persist regarding whether switchbacks can be described with Ideal MHD (magnetohydrodynamic) physics or Hall-MHD physics and whether their origin is at the solar surface or in the solar wind. To settle these controversies, we present Parker Solar Probe electric field measurements between 13 and 40 solar radii, which show that switchbacks have non-zero electric fields in the plasma frame, a finding that definitively settles the physics controversy by proving that switchbacks are Hall-MHD, not Ideal MHD, structures. Along with these electric fields, there are enhanced Poynting vectors having three components with similar magnitudes that exist only inside the switchbacks. These facts contradict the view of switchbacks as simple outward-propagating pulses. Together, they resolve one controversy by showing that switchbacks in the young solar wind are a non-MHD process. They contribute to the second (source) controversy by identifying switchbacks as sites of active, in-situ, evolution. These findings provide a new framework for understanding energy transport and dissipation in astrophysical plasmas.

AI.tldr: Using Parker Solar Probe electric field measurements (13-40 solar radii), the paper proves that magnetic switchbacks are Hall-MHD (not Ideal MHD) structures, resolving a fundamental physics controversy, and shows they are sites of active in-situ evolution, challenging the view of simple outward-propagating pulses.
AI.motivation: To settle two fundamental controversies: whether switchbacks are described by Ideal MHD or Hall-MHD physics, and whether their origin is at the solar surface or in the solar wind.
AI.method: Analysis of Parker Solar Probe electric field measurements between 13 and 40 solar radii, examining electric fields in the plasma frame and Poynting vectors within switchbacks.
AI.result: Switchbacks have non-zero electric fields in the plasma frame (proving Hall-MHD, not Ideal MHD), and exhibit enhanced three-component Poynting vectors exclusively inside switchbacks, contradicting the simple outward-propagating pulse model.
AI.conclusion: Switchbacks in the young solar wind are a non-MHD process (Hall-MHD) and are sites of active in-situ evolution, providing a new framework for understanding energy transport and dissipation in astrophysical plasmas.

title: A new sample of Little Red Dots at $z<0.45$ in DESI DR1: Broad Balmer lines, low ionization spectrum and no variability
comment: 21 pages, 17 figures, submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: JWST has unveiled an abundant population of compact broad-line emitters largely at $z\gtrsim4$, the Little Red Dots (LRDs), which might represent a previously unprobed supermassive black hole evolution channel predominant at high redshift. However, the LRDs have remained mostly elusive at lower redshift ($z\lesssim2$) where detailed studies are possible from ground-based observatories. We searched for low-redshift LRDs in the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) survey. Our search is primarily based on emission line properties, as opposed to earlier approaches that searched for compact sources with specific photometric spectral energy distributions. We report the discovery of eight LRDs at $z=0.2-0.45$, which show spectral features akin to the high-redshift LRDs in the rest-frame optical. The sources are characterized by broad Balmer lines, steep Balmer decrements, compact morphologies, Balmer absorption features and/or strong He I emission, but weak or absent He II, [Ne V] or other high excitation lines typical of Type I AGN. For 7 out of 8 sources, we retrieve dense-cadence light curves from time-domain surveys and for most sources we find weak to no intrinsic variability ($0.0-0.1$ mag) over $4-17$ years in the rest-frame. We also highlight the identification of a quasar with similar Balmer line profiles as LRDs, but shows differences in Balmer decrement, significant variability, and high-ionisation lines. Given the effective volume $4.9{\rm Gpc^3}$ covered by DESI DR1 at $z<0.45$, our sample corresponds to a number density of $1.6\times10^{-9}$Mpc$^{-3}$, indicating a number density $\sim$10,000 times lower than in the first billion years of cosmic time. We find a dearth of luminous and red LRDs at $z<1$ compared to higher-redshift, which could suggest lower gas feeding rates of LRD activity due to higher metallicities at later cosmic epochs.

AI.tldr: JWST discovered numerous high-redshift (z>4) Little Red Dots (LRDs), but few were known at lower redshifts. Using DESI data, this study identified 8 LRDs at z=0.2-0.45 with similar spectral features to high-z LRDs. These sources show broad Balmer lines, steep Balmer decrements, compact morphologies, and weak variability. Their number density at low-z (~1.6×10⁻⁹ Mpc⁻³) is ~10,000 times lower than at high-z, suggesting a dearth of luminous red LRDs at z<1 possibly due to higher metallicities reducing gas feeding rates.
AI.motivation: To find low-redshift (z<2) analogues of the abundant high-redshift Little Red Dots (LRDs) discovered by JWST, enabling detailed ground-based follow-up studies that are feasible only at lower redshifts.
AI.method: Searched DESI survey using emission line properties (rather than photometric SEDs) to identify LRDs at z=0.2-0.45; analyzed spectra, light curves from time-domain surveys, and computed number densities.
AI.result: Discovered 8 LRDs at z=0.2-0.45 with broad Balmer lines, steep Balmer decrements, compact morphologies, Balmer absorption/He I emission, weak high-ionization lines, and weak variability (0.0-0.1 mag over 4-17 yr). Number density at low-z is ~10,000× lower than at z>4.
AI.conclusion: Low-redshift LRDs exist but are extremely rare compared to high redshift, suggesting a strong evolution in LRD population. The dearth at z<1 may be due to higher metallicities reducing gas feeding rates of LRD activity in later cosmic epochs.

title: Toward a Comprehensive Grid of Cepheid Models with MESA. IV. Modest Effects of Rotation on Blue Loops
comment: Accepted for publication in Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series
summary: Evolutionary tracks for $2-8M_\odot$ stars, with metallicities of $Z=0.014$, $0.006$, and $0.002$, including rotation, are computed with Modules for Experiments in Stellar Astrophysics (MESA). We study how rotation impacts the evolutionary properties of classical Cepheids. We examine whether rotation can offer a plausible explanation for the mass discrepancy problem when it is included in the evolutionary code using the fully diffusive approximation for rotationally induced mixing processes. We find that rotation barely influences the appearance and luminosity levels of the blue loops. While luminosity increases with increasing initial rotation rate, the increase does not exceed 0.04 dex, a fraction of the increase resulting from including the main sequence (MS) core overshooting of $0.2H_p$. As a consequence, rotation alone cannot resolve the mass discrepancy problem without simultaneously requiring significant MS core overshooting. Similar to the mass-luminosity relation, the period-radius and period-luminosity relations are barely affected by rotation, while the period-age relation predicts Cepheid ages to be only a few per cent longer compared with models without rotation. The predicted surface rotational velocities are too large compared with observations. These results are in contrast with those obtained with the Geneva code, which implements rotational mixing using the advective-diffusive scheme. In that approach, the luminosity levels of the loops are significantly higher, their luminosity extent increases, and the predicted rotation velocities are lower, compared with MESA models. The differences between the two approaches arise from significantly more efficient rotation-induced mixing during the MS evolution in models computed with the advective-diffusive scheme.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the effects of rotation on the evolution of classical Cepheids (2-8 M☉) using MESA models, finding that rotation alone (with diffusive mixing) cannot resolve the mass discrepancy problem, unlike Geneva code results using advective-diffusive mixing which show stronger rotational effects.
AI.motivation: To examine whether rotation can explain the mass discrepancy problem in classical Cepheids, where evolutionary masses are systematically lower than pulsation masses.
AI.method: Evolutionary tracks for 2-8 M☉ stars at Z=0.014, 0.006, 0.002 were computed using MESA with rotation implemented via the fully diffusive approximation for rotationally induced mixing.
AI.result: Rotation barely affects blue loops, luminosity increases by <0.04 dex (much less than 0.2Hp core overshooting). Rotation alone cannot resolve the mass discrepancy. Period-radius, period-luminosity relations are barely affected. Predicted rotational velocities are too high compared to observations. Results differ significantly from Geneva code (advective-diffusive scheme) which shows stronger rotational effects.
AI.conclusion: Rotation with diffusive mixing cannot resolve the Cepheid mass discrepancy without significant MS core overshooting. The choice of rotational mixing implementation (diffusive vs. advective-diffusive) critically affects results.

title: Reconstructing the Stripping History of the Sagittarius Stream with Neural Networks
comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, accepted for Publication in ApJ
summary: The Sagittarius (Sgr) Stream is produced by the ongoing disruption of the Sgr dwarf spheroidal (dSph) galaxy and is thought to contain multiple wraps that were stripped during different pericentric passages. In this study, we introduce a neural-network--based method trained on $N$-body simulations to infer the stripping time of Sgr Stream stars directly from their phase-space coordinates. We combine spectroscopic data from SEGUE, APOGEE DR17, and LAMOST DR7 LRS with \textit{Gaia} EDR3 astrometry and distance estimates from the latest \texttt{StarHorse} catalog to identify high-quality Sgr Stream members. Applying our method to these stars, we measure a clear metallicity gradient with stripping time, well described by a linear relation with slope $\sim 0.3~\mathrm{dex~Gyr^{-1}}$. We further predict the stripping times of globular clusters previously suggested to originate from the Sgr dSph. M 54, Terzan 7, Terzan 8, and Arp 2 exhibit stripping times consistent with being currently bound to the Sgr remnant. Pal 12, Whiting 1, and NGC 2419 are inferred to have been stripped $0.9 \pm 0.1$, $1.1 \pm 0.2$, and $2.1 \pm 0.2$ Gyr ago, respectively. For NGC 4147 and NGC 5634, whose membership in the Sgr system remains uncertain, our analysis suggests stripping times of $1.1 \pm 0.4$ and $1.1 \pm 0.1$ Gyr, respectively, if they are ultimately confirmed as genuine Sgr members. These results demonstrate that data-driven models of dynamical stripping histories offer a promising approach for reconstructing the formation and chemical evolution of the Sgr Stream.

AI.tldr: The paper uses a neural-network method trained on N-body simulations to infer the stripping times of Sagittarius Stream stars from phase-space coordinates, identifying a clear metallicity gradient (~0.3 dex/Gyr) and predicting stripping times for several globular clusters associated with the Sgr dwarf spheroidal galaxy.
AI.motivation: To reconstruct the dynamical stripping history and chemical evolution of the Sagittarius Stream by inferring when stars were stripped from the Sgr dSph galaxy, using a data-driven approach that overcomes limitations of traditional dynamical modeling.
AI.method: A neural-network-based method trained on N-body simulations infers stripping times from phase-space coordinates. High-quality Sgr Stream members are identified using combined spectroscopic data (SEGUE, APOGEE DR17, LAMOST DR7 LRS), Gaia EDR3 astrometry, and StarHorse distance estimates.
AI.result: A clear metallicity gradient of ~0.3 dex/Gyr with stripping time is found. Stripping times are predicted for globular clusters: Pal 12 (0.9±0.1 Gyr), Whiting 1 (1.1±0.2 Gyr), NGC 2419 (2.1±0.2 Gyr), and tentatively for NGC 4147 (1.1±0.4 Gyr) and NGC 5634 (1.1±0.1 Gyr). M 54, Terzan 7, Terzan 8, and Arp 2 are consistent with being currently bound.
AI.conclusion: Data-driven models of dynamical stripping histories are a promising approach for reconstructing the formation and chemical evolution of the Sgr Stream, enabling new insights into the assembly history of the Milky Way through its satellite interactions.

title: The Distribution of Blue Straggler Stars in the Color-Magnitude Diagrams of Old Open Clusters
comment: 31 pages, 8 figures
summary: We examine the blue straggler star (BSS) populations of six old ($\geq$4 Gyr) open clusters: M67, NGC 188, NGC 6791, Berkeley 32, Berkeley 39, and Trumpler 19. We find that 50% of BSSs have color-magnitude diagram (CMD) locations corresponding to single stars in the final third of their main-sequence lifetimes. This build-up of BSSs near the terminal-age main sequence (TAMS) is primarily, but not solely, driven by more massive BSSs. Eleven of the BSSs have white dwarf companions with measured cooling ages; their evolution age distributions indicate that more massive BSSs typically form far from the zero-age main sequence, whereas lower mass BSSs can form at every evolutionary age. We show that inferred core helium amounts (above primordial) of late-evolution-age BSSs correspond to the core helium fused by cluster main-sequence stars near the turnoffs. We also find that the masses of asymptotic giant branch (AGB) mass-transfer BSSs require evolved main-sequence accretors and conservative mass transfer. These findings indicate that helium enrichment of progenitor accretors leads to the prevalence of BSSs near the TAMS. We further classify the evolutionary stages of the progenitor donors in M67 and NGC 188 and find mass transfer during the AGB accounts for at least half of the BSSs. We trace how the main-sequence binary population of NGC 188 evolves, and find that only 30-40% of interacting binaries create BSSs and that progenitor orbits must change to match current BSS periods.

AI.tldr: Study of blue straggler stars in six old open clusters finds 50% cluster near terminal-age main sequence, linked to helium enrichment from mass transfer, with AGB donors accounting for at least half of BSSs.
AI.motivation: To understand the formation mechanisms and evolutionary pathways of blue straggler stars in old open clusters, particularly their concentration near the terminal-age main sequence.
AI.method: Analysis of color-magnitude diagram positions, white dwarf companion cooling ages, core helium abundance estimates, and binary population evolution modeling for six old open clusters (M67, NGC 188, NGC 6791, Berkeley 32, Berkeley 39, Trumpler 19).
AI.result: 50% of BSSs are in the final third of main-sequence lifetimes; more massive BSSs form far from ZAMS while lower mass BSSs form at all evolutionary ages; core helium enrichment from progenitor accretion drives TAMS clustering; AGB mass transfer accounts for ≥50% of BSSs in M67 and NGC 188; only 30-40% of interacting binaries produce BSSs.
AI.conclusion: Helium enrichment of accretor progenitors through mass transfer explains the prevalence of BSSs near the TAMS, and the formation efficiency of BSSs from interacting binaries is relatively low (30-40%).

title: An Updated Characterization of Luminous Lyα emitters at the End of Reionization
comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, submitted to ApJL, comments welcome
summary: We present a multi-wavelength physical characterization of 14 luminous Ly$α$ emitters (LAEs) at $z\approx6$, integrating deep ground-based Magellan/M2FS spectroscopy with heterogeneous JWST/NIRCam broad- and medium-band imaging. Identified via strong Ly$α$ lines with extreme Ly$α$ luminosities of ${>}10^{42.6}$ erg s$^{-1}$, the sample exhibits very large rest-frame equivalent widths (${\gtrsim}100$ Å) and steeply blue UV continua ($β_{\rm median}\simeq-2.2$, $-18.2>M_{\rm 1500}>-20.2$ mag). Crucially, the integration of NIRCam medium-band photometry (F410M) breaks the degeneracy between strong rest-optical nebular emission and Balmer breaks, resolving prior mass overestimations. The tightly constrained spectral energy distribution modeling demonstrates that these luminous LAEs tend to be unequivocally low-mass, ultra-young dwarf starbursts; half the sample is characterized by stellar masses of $M_* < 10^8 M_{\odot}$, ages $\lesssim10$ Myr, and negligible dust attenuation. We also map the production efficiency of ionizing photons and Ly$α$ escape fractions ($f_{\rm esc}^{\rm Lyα}$). The $f_{\rm esc}^{\rm Lyα}$ values are exceptionally high, with a median of ${\gtrsim}40$%, increasing for the bluer UV continua. Finally, analyzing spatial offsets between the Ly$α$ centroid and the stellar counterpart, we demonstrate empirically that internal dust content, rather than neutral hydrogen gas, dominate the suppression of Ly$α$ radiative transfer. Our study reveals that strong Ly$α$ emission of the luminous LAEs are generally attributed to both the vigorous starburst activities and the high $f_{\rm esc}^{\rm Lyα}$. Resembling Lyman continuum leakers, these extreme dwarf systems function as highly efficient ionizing engines at the conclusion of the Epoch of Reionization.

AI.tldr: This paper characterizes 14 luminous Lyα emitters (LAEs) at z≈6 using Magellan/M2FS spectroscopy and JWST/NIRCam imaging. These are ultra-young, low-mass dwarf starbursts (half with M* < 10^8 M⊙, ages <10 Myr) with extreme Lyα luminosities, high Lyα escape fractions (median >40%), and negligible dust. Medium-band NIRCam photometry resolves previous mass overestimations. The study shows Lyα suppression is dominated by internal dust, not neutral hydrogen, and these systems resemble Lyman continuum leakers acting as efficient ionizing engines at the end of reionization.
AI.motivation: To physically characterize luminous LAEs at z≈6, resolving degeneracies in SED modeling (e.g., nebular emission vs. Balmer breaks) that previously led to mass overestimations, and to understand the drivers of strong Lyα emission and its escape mechanisms.
AI.method: Multi-wavelength analysis combining deep Magellan/M2FS spectroscopy with JWST/NIRCam broad- and medium-band (F410M) photometry for 14 LAEs at z≈6, enabling SED modeling, Lyα escape fraction measurements, and spatial offset analysis between Lyα centroid and stellar counterpart.
AI.result: Luminous LAEs are ultra-young, low-mass dwarf starbursts (half with M* < 10^8 M⊙, ages <10 Myr, negligible dust). Lyα escape fractions are exceptionally high (median >40%), increasing with bluer UV continua. Internal dust, not neutral hydrogen, dominates Lyα radiative transfer suppression. These systems resemble Lyman continuum leakers.
AI.conclusion: Strong Lyα emission in luminous LAEs is driven by both vigorous starburst activity and high Lyα escape fractions. These extreme dwarf systems act as highly efficient ionizing engines at the end of the Epoch of Reionization.

title: The Close Binary V486 Carinae
comment: 17 pages, 15 figures, accepted by MNRAS
summary: The hitherto neglected close binary V486 Car is studied with the aid of newly applied satellite photometry (HIPPARCOS and TESS), high dispersion spectrometry (HERCULES) and ground-based B and V photometry. While the sinusoidal light variations are suggestive of a near-contact system, the stars have only shallow eclipse, so highly confident parametrization becomes challenging. We find: $M_1 = 2.1 \pm 0.1$, $M_2 = 0.4 \pm 0.1$; $R_1 = 3.20 \pm 0.02$, $R_2 = 1.48 \pm 0.01$; (${\odot}$); $T_{e1} = 10000 \pm 500$, $T_{e2} = 6200 \pm 200$ (K); distance = 162 $\pm$ 12 (pc). New times of minima for V486 Car have been examined, including recent observations from TESS. The role of the relatively significant O'Connell effect is examined. As well as the conspicuous asymmetry from the main effect of about 0.036 mag (V), a jitter, with amplitude of about 0.005 V mag and quasi-period of order $\sim$ 10 d is noticed. There is a tendency for such photometric excursions at one maximum to precede those at the other. As well, the O -- C data indicate the presence of a low mass star $\sim$0.3 M$_{\odot}$ in an orbit separated by a few AU from the close binary. More accurate and plentiful spectroscopic data would be requisite for further investigations. A brief discussion reviews possible approaches to understanding the system in the context of near-contact binary scenarios.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the close binary system V486 Car using satellite photometry (HIPPARCOS, TESS), high-dispersion spectrometry (HERCULES), and ground-based photometry. It finds stellar masses (2.1, 0.4 M⊙), radii (3.20, 1.48 R⊙), effective temperatures (10000, 6200 K), and a distance of 162 pc. The system shows an O'Connell effect (0.036 mag asymmetry), photometric jitter (~0.005 mag, ~10-day quasi-period), and O-C data suggesting a low-mass (~0.3 M⊙) third body at a few AU separation.
AI.motivation: To analyze the hitherto neglected close binary V486 Car using newly available multi-wavelength data, aiming to derive its fundamental stellar parameters and understand its evolutionary state as a near-contact binary system.
AI.method: Satellite photometry (HIPPARCOS and TESS), high-dispersion spectrometry (HERCULES), and ground-based B and V photometry were applied. Light curve analysis, O-C diagram analysis, and examination of the O'Connell effect and photometric jitter were performed.
AI.result: Masses: M1=2.1±0.1, M2=0.4±0.1 M⊙; Radii: R1=3.20±0.02, R2=1.48±0.01 R⊙; Teff: 10000±500, 6200±200 K; Distance: 162±12 pc. O'Connell effect of 0.036 mag asymmetry and quasi-periodic jitter (~0.005 mag, ~10 days) detected. O-C data indicate a third body (~0.3 M⊙) at a few AU.
AI.conclusion: The system is a near-contact binary with shallow eclipses. A low-mass tertiary companion is inferred. More accurate and plentiful spectroscopic data are needed for further investigations.

title: Observation of spontaneous N-bearing PAH formation using ion trap: a new formation pathway in the interstellar medium
summary: Nitrogen-bearing polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (N-PAHs) are key precursors to complex organic molecules in both the interstellar medium and the nitrogen-rich planetary atmospheres. Despite the recent detections of nitrogen-functionalized astromolecules, their formation pathways remain an open question. The discrepancies between their predicted and observed abundances point to unknown mechanism that govern their evolution in the astrophysical environments. Employing an ion trap technique and electronic structure calculations, we unravel multiple barrier-less reactions between gas-phase pyrimidine cations (C$_4$H$_4$N$_2^+$) and acetylene (C$_2$H$_2$) which form an hitherto unreported endocyclic- N-PAHs (C$_8$H$_7$N$_2^+$). The present measurements on reactions involving a double-nitrogen subsituted aromatic heterocycle have implications to the astrochemistry of both the Titan's atmosphere and interstellar medium.

AI.tldr: This paper reveals barrier-less reactions between pyrimidine cations and acetylene forming endocyclic N-PAHs, with implications for astrochemistry in Titan's atmosphere and the interstellar medium.
AI.motivation: Discrepancies between predicted and observed abundances of nitrogen-functionalized astromolecules point to unknown formation mechanisms governing their evolution in astrophysical environments.
AI.method: Ion trap technique combined with electronic structure calculations to study gas-phase reactions between pyrimidine cations (C₄H₄N₂⁺) and acetylene (C₂H₂).
AI.result: Multiple barrier-less reactions were discovered that form previously unreported endocyclic N-PAHs (C₈H₇N₂⁺) from pyrimidine cations and acetylene.
AI.conclusion: These findings on double-nitrogen substituted aromatic heterocycle reactions have significant implications for astrochemistry in both Titan's nitrogen-rich atmosphere and the interstellar medium.

title: Luminaries in the Sky: The TESS LEGACY Sample of Bright Stars. II. In-depth seismic characterisation of 32 naked-eye stars in the PLATO LOP fields
comment: Under revision for Astronomy & Astrophysics. The abstract has been shortened for arXiv. 22 pages, 5 figures in the main text, and 29 figures in the appendices
summary: The NASA TESS mission is conducting a nearly full-sky survey, enabling the photometric characterisation of millions of stars. The forthcoming ESA PLATO mission will provide long-duration, high-precision photometry of tens of thousands of bright stars to be characterised through asteroseismology. The TESS Luminaries Sample is a catalogue of 196 bright naked-eye (V < 6) main-sequence (MS) and sub-giant (SG) stars exhibiting solar-like oscillations. Among them, the subset located within the PLATO Long-duration Observation Phase (LOP) fields constitutes an exceptional set of targets that will be observable by PLATO from the earliest phases of the mission, making them ideal calibrators during commissioning and the first months of science operations. This paper aims to provide an in-depth asteroseismic characterisation of 32 Luminaries stars that fall within the PLATO LOP fields of view. Individual mode parameters were extracted for the first time for 26 of them. We used three independent seismic pipelines, one of which is similar to the algorithms used in the official PLATO pipeline. Statistical criterion were applied to identify the optimal combination of data calibration, observing cadence, and fitting pipeline for each star. For all stars, we derived large and small separations, the asymptotic phase term, radial mode amplitudes, and mean linewidths per order. Comparisons reveal consistent trends in the seismic parameters, confirming the robustness of our analysis. In sub-giants, mixed-mode identification differs in the three pipelines, revealing extraction inconsistencies requiring longer datasets to improve our mode identifications. The Luminaries stars located in the PLATO LOP fields constitute a unique sample that will play a crucial role in validating, calibrating, and optimising PLATO's seismic performance.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an in-depth asteroseismic characterization of 32 bright, naked-eye stars from the TESS Luminaries Sample located within PLATO's Long-duration Observation Phase fields, using three independent seismic pipelines to extract mode parameters, with most stars (26/32) characterized for the first time.
AI.motivation: To provide early calibrators and validation targets for the upcoming ESA PLATO mission by asteroseismically characterizing bright stars observable from PLATO's earliest phases.
AI.method: Three independent seismic pipelines (one akin to PLATO's official pipeline) were used to extract individual mode parameters from 32 Luminaries stars in PLATO LOP fields, applying statistical criteria to select optimal calibration, cadence, and pipeline combinations.
AI.result: Derived large and small separations, asymptotic phase term, radial mode amplitudes, and mean linewidths per order for all 32 stars; first-time mode extraction for 26 stars; consistent trends across pipelines confirm robustness, though mixed-mode identification in sub-giants showed inconsistencies requiring longer datasets.
AI.conclusion: The Luminaries stars in PLATO LOP fields are a unique sample that will be crucial for validating, calibrating, and optimizing PLATO's seismic performance from the earliest mission phases.

title: Self-Interacting Dark Matter in Brown Dwarfs
comment: 20 pages, 7 figures
summary: Brown dwarfs, being transitional objects between giant planets and low-mass stars, possess dense, cool interiors that provide optimal conditions to explore non-standard physics. Capture and accumulation of dark-matter particles can alter the thermal, structural and dynamic of these substellar objects. We aim to apply a self-consistent two-fluid framework to model the internal structure of self-gravitating brown dwarfs and to quantify how the presence of a dark-matter component modifies their mass--radius relations and dynamical properties. The brown dwarf is modeled as a composite system of a baryonic fluid, described by a polytropic equation of state, and an independent dark-matter fluid. Both components are coupled through their shared gravitational potential in hydrostatic equilibrium. We solve numerically the coupled Lane-Emden equations for a range of dark-matter mass fractions. We find that dark matter accumulating in the core reshapes the baryonic density profile, modifying both the radius and the second-order Love number. Radius and dynamical anomalies in brown dwarfs can serve as diagnostic tools to constrain dark-matter properties. Future high-precision astrometric missions could identify these structural signatures, establishing brown dwarfs as possible detectors of dark matter in the Galaxy.

AI.tldr: This paper models brown dwarfs as two-fluid systems (baryonic + dark matter) using coupled Lane-Emden equations, finding that accumulated dark matter alters their mass-radius relations and Love numbers, potentially enabling brown dwarfs to serve as dark matter detectors.
AI.motivation: Brown dwarfs possess dense, cool interiors that provide optimal conditions to explore non-standard physics, specifically the capture and accumulation of dark-matter particles which can alter their thermal, structural, and dynamic properties.
AI.method: A self-consistent two-fluid framework models the brown dwarf as a composite system of a baryonic fluid (polytropic equation of state) and an independent dark-matter fluid, coupled through their shared gravitational potential in hydrostatic equilibrium. The coupled Lane-Emden equations are solved numerically for a range of dark-matter mass fractions.
AI.result: Dark matter accumulating in the core reshapes the baryonic density profile, modifying both the radius and the second-order Love number of the brown dwarf.
AI.conclusion: Radius and dynamical anomalies in brown dwarfs can serve as diagnostic tools to constrain dark-matter properties. Future high-precision astrometric missions could identify these structural signatures, establishing brown dwarfs as possible detectors of dark matter in the Galaxy.

title: Discovery of a Compact Hub-Filament System in G286.21+0.17 with JWST and ALMA: Insights into Protocluster Formation and Competitive Accretion
summary: We present a multi-wavelength study of the massive protocluster G286.21+0.17 (G286) using \emph{JWST} near-infrared imaging and ALMA H$^{13}$CO$^{+}$(1--0) observations. The \emph{JWST} images uncover a compact ($\sim$0.5 pc) hub-filament system (HFS), comprising a dense central hub connected by at least four converging filaments seen in absorption, along with multiple H$_2$ protostellar jets/outflows. The hub hosts dense core G286c1. The H$^{13}$CO$^{+}$ emission confirms this HFS over [$-$19.2, $-$16.4]~km~s$^{-1}$. The \emph{JWST} images further trace prominent photodissociation regions around the H\,{\sc ii}~region~A, powered by a B-type star. The radial distribution of ALMAGAL 1.38 mm core properties reveals steep power-law slopes toward the hub center. Within the inner hub (r < 8'', $\sim0.1$~pc), the core number density follows $ρ~[\rm pc^{-2}] \propto r^{-2.4\pm0.5}$, the surface density scales as $Σ~[\rm g~cm^{-2}] \propto r^{-1.0\pm0.2}$, and the enclosed core mass varies as $M_{\rm core}~[M_{\odot}] \propto r^{-1.2\pm0.2}$, while core diameters remain approximately constant ($D_{\rm core}~[\rm AU] \propto r^{-0.1\pm0.1}$). These trends, along with filament mass accretion rates of $7\times10^{-6}$--$1.8\times10^{-4}$~$M_\odot$~yr$^{-1}$, support a competitive accretion scenario in which gravitational focusing enhances core growth toward the hub center. Filament linewidths increase from tail/outer-region to head/hub-region, consistent with gravity-driven turbulence. However, the absence of a preferred alignment between velocity gradients and gravitational force directions may indicate a dynamically evolved system. The HFS likely formed through large-scale gas layer interactions and compression by the adjacent H\,{\sc ii} region. Overall, star formation in G286 appears regulated by filamentary accretion, competitive core growth in the hub, and stellar feedback.

AI.tldr: JWST and ALMA observations of the massive protocluster G286.21+0.17 reveal a compact hub-filament system (HFS) with converging filaments, protostellar jets, and a dense central hub. Core properties show steep radial power-law slopes (number density ∝ r⁻²·⁴, surface density ∝ r⁻¹·⁰, enclosed mass ∝ r⁻¹·²) supporting competitive accretion. Filament mass accretion rates (7×10⁻⁶–1.8×10⁻⁴ M⊙ yr⁻¹) and gravity-driven turbulence are evident, but misaligned velocity gradients suggest a dynamically evolved system. The HFS likely formed via gas layer interactions and HII region compression, with star formation regulated by filamentary accretion, competitive core growth, and stellar feedback.
AI.motivation: To investigate the early stages of massive star and cluster formation by studying the multi-scale structure, kinematics, and core properties of the hub-filament system in G286.21+0.17, combining high-resolution JWST near-infrared and ALMA molecular line observations.
AI.method: Multi-wavelength observational study using JWST near-infrared imaging (tracing absorption features, H₂ jets/outflows, and PDRs) and ALMA H¹³CO⁺(1–0) line emission (tracing dense gas kinematics and filament structure), along with ALMAGAL 1.38 mm continuum core catalog to derive radial distributions of core properties.
AI.result: (1) JWST reveals a compact (~0.5 pc) hub-filament system with ≥4 converging absorption filaments, H₂ jets/outflows, and PDRs around an HII region powered by a B-type star. (2) H¹³CO⁺ confirms the HFS over velocity range [−19.2, −16.4] km s⁻¹. (3) Core radial profiles in the inner hub (r<0.1 pc) show steep power-law slopes: ρ ∝ r⁻²·⁴, Σ ∝ r⁻¹·⁰, Mcore ∝ r⁻¹·², Dcore ∝ r⁻⁰·¹. (4) Filament mass accretion rates = 7×10⁻⁶–1.8×10⁻⁴ M⊙ yr⁻¹. (5) Filament linewidths increase from tail to hub, but velocity gradients lack preferred alignment with gravitational forces.
AI.conclusion: The hub-filament system in G286 supports a competitive accretion scenario where gravitational focusing enhances core growth toward the hub center. Gravity-driven turbulence is present, but the misaligned velocity gradients indicate a dynamically evolved system. The HFS likely formed via large-scale gas layer interactions and compression by an adjacent HII region, with star formation regulated by filamentary accretion, competitive core growth, and stellar feedback.

title: The Role of Magnetic Reconnection in Energizing Protons and Heavier Ions at the Heliospheric Current Sheet
comment: 14 pages, 3 figures. Accepted in ApJ as of May 13, 2026
summary: During near-Sun crossings of the heliospheric current sheet (HCS), Parker Solar Probe (PSP) observed populations of high-energy protons and heavier ions indicating possible energization by magnetic reconnection up to 10s -- 100s keV nucleon$^{-1}$. Here we study ion acceleration by magnetic reconnection at the HCS. To estimate ion energization, we solve the Parker transport equation coupled to a large-scale 2D MHD reconnection simulation. We find that multiple ion species develop power-law distributions with both spectral index and high-energy cutoff $E_{\text{max}}$ consistent with in-situ data. By accounting for the injection physics determined by kinetic simulations, we confirm that the charge-to-mass ratio scales as $E_{\text{max}} \propto (Q/M)^α$ with $α\sim 0.8-1.1$, approximately consistent with PSP measurements in the broader range $α\sim 0.6-1.7$. In the limit where ions are injected at the same energy per nucleon, $α$ can be as low as $\sim 0.3$. These findings further support the role of magnetic reconnection in producing high-energy heavy ions at the HCS.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates ion acceleration by magnetic reconnection at the heliospheric current sheet (HCS) using MHD simulations coupled with the Parker transport equation, finding that multiple ion species develop power-law distributions with spectral indices and high-energy cutoffs consistent with Parker Solar Probe observations, and confirming charge-to-mass ratio scaling of Emax ∝ (Q/M)^α with α ~ 0.8-1.1.
AI.motivation: Understanding the mechanism behind high-energy proton and heavy ion populations (10s–100s keV/nucleon) observed by Parker Solar Probe during near-Sun crossings of the heliospheric current sheet, specifically testing whether magnetic reconnection can account for the energization.
AI.method: Solving the Parker transport equation coupled to a large-scale 2D MHD reconnection simulation, incorporating injection physics determined by kinetic simulations, to estimate ion energization for multiple species.
AI.result: Multiple ion species develop power-law distributions with spectral indices and high-energy cutoff Emax consistent with PSP in-situ data. The charge-to-mass ratio scaling exponent α ~ 0.8-1.1 matches PSP measurements (broader range α ~ 0.6-1.7). Under same energy-per-nucleon injection, α can be as low as ~0.3.
AI.conclusion: Magnetic reconnection at the HCS can produce the observed high-energy heavy ions, further supporting its role in particle energization in the near-Sun environment.

title: Boundary-supported radial layering in Hoag-like ring galaxies
comment: 5 pages, 3 figures; submitted to MNRAS Letters
summary: Clean Hoag-like ring galaxies are often characterized by an old compact central component, a depleted gap, and a detached outer ring. We identify a boundary-supported radial-layering mechanism in a shell-deformed Kepler control model. A compact inner boundary supplies the core state, while a localized effective shell deformation, interpreted as the reduced imprint of externally supplied material settled near a finite circularization radius, needs to create only an internal maximum and a subsequent outer minimum. These act as the gap barrier and ring-supporting well. The onset of this structure is organized by a saddle-node threshold of the critical-point equation. In a 10^4-point Monte Carlo scan, shell-localized boundary-supported candidates occupy finite parameter volume under the adopted priors, and none of the localized candidates contains an ordered interior minimum--maximum--minimum subsequence. The same branch gives a scale-free gap-to-ring interval overlapping representative ratios for Hoag's Object, UGC 4599, and PGC 1000714, but not for the environmentally processed comparison object JO171.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a boundary-supported radial-layering mechanism in a shell-deformed Kepler model to explain the formation of clean Hoag-like ring galaxies, where a compact inner boundary provides the core, and a localized shell deformation creates a gap barrier and ring-supporting well. The mechanism is organized by a saddle-node threshold, and Monte Carlo simulations show it occupies finite parameter volume. The scale-free gap-to-ring interval matches observations for Hoag's Object, UGC 4599, and PGC 1000714, but not for JO171.
AI.motivation: To explain the formation mechanism of clean Hoag-like ring galaxies characterized by an old compact core, a depleted gap, and a detached outer ring, where no ordered interior minimum-maximum-minimum subsequence is observed.
AI.method: A boundary-supported radial-layering mechanism is identified in a shell-deformed Kepler control model, using a compact inner boundary and localized effective shell deformation. A 10^4-point Monte Carlo scan is performed, and results are compared against observational data for Hoag's Object, UGC 4599, PGC 1000714, and JO171.
AI.result: Shell-localized boundary-supported candidates occupy finite parameter volume under adopted priors; none contains an ordered interior minimum-maximum-minimum subsequence. The scale-free gap-to-ring interval overlaps with Hoag's Object, UGC 4599, and PGC 1000714, but not with the environmentally processed comparison object JO171.
AI.conclusion: The proposed mechanism successfully reproduces the structural features of clean Hoag-like ring galaxies, distinguishing them from environmentally processed objects like JO171, and suggests a saddle-node threshold organizes the onset of this structure.

title: Analysing the highly irregular boundaries of solar pores
comment: Submitted to A&A
summary: Solar pores possess irregular and evolving boundaries that are often far from the ideal circular flux tubes assumed in many magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) oscillation models. To tackle this irregularity in a consistent way for wave analysis, we introduce a framework that employs the convex hull of the pore boundary - derived from intensity minimum error thresholding - as the domain to perform further analysis. Using the modal assurance criterion, we find the range of pore shapes for which this approximation is valid. We demonstrate the usefulness of this framework by applying it to multi-height, high-cadence observations (4170 angstrom continuum, G-band, Na~\textsc{i}, and Ca~\textsc{ii}~K) of a solar pore, and apply Proper Orthogonal Decomposition of the convex hull to determine wave modes. The fundamental sausage ($m=1$) and kink ($m=2$) mode is found to remain reliable, while higher-order fluting modes ($m\ge3$) are strongly degraded by small-scale boundary irregularity. As expected, sausage-like modes dominate the variance at all heights and exhibit a systematic upward shift in frequency, consistent with freely propagating compressive waves. In contrast, the kink-like motions appear weak, confined to a persistent low-frequency peak, and most plausibly interpreted as a forced response to granular buffeting rather than a propagating mode. Together, these results establish a practical methodology for boundary-mode analysis in real, highly structured pores and provide new constraints on the nature and height evolution of MHD waves in the lower solar atmosphere.

AI.tldr: The authors develop a convex hull-based framework to analyze MHD wave modes in solar pores with irregular boundaries, finding that sausage (m=1) and kink (m=2) modes remain reliable but higher-order fluting modes (m≥3) are degraded, with sausage modes dominating and kink modes appearing as forced responses to granular buffeting.
AI.motivation: Solar pores have irregular, evolving boundaries that deviate from ideal circular flux tube models used in MHD oscillation studies, necessitating a consistent analytical framework for wave analysis in realistic pore geometries.
AI.method: Convex hull approximation of pore boundaries from intensity minimum error thresholding; Modal Assurance Criterion to validate shape approximations; Proper Orthogonal Decomposition applied to multi-height (4170Å, G-band, Na I, Ca II K) high-cadence observations.
AI.result: Sausage (m=1) and kink (m=2) modes remain reliable; higher-order fluting modes (m≥3) are degraded by small-scale boundary irregularity; sausage modes dominate variance at all heights with upward frequency shift (compressive waves); kink modes are weak, confined to low-frequency peak, interpreted as forced response to granular buffeting.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a practical methodology for boundary-mode analysis in real pores and yields new constraints on MHD wave nature and height evolution in the lower solar atmosphere.

title: DREAMS. JWST Spectroscopy of a $z=8.3$ Galaxy with an ALMA Dust Continuum Detection: Early Dust, Very High $T_{\rm dust}$, and a Multi-wavelength [OIII] Ratio Discrepancy
comment: 18 pages, 18 figure, Submitted to ApJ
summary: We present a deep DREAMS JWST/NIRSpec MSA medium-grating spectrum of MACS0416-Y1, a galaxy at $z=8.312$ with the highest-redshift ALMA dust continuum detection to date, in order to characterize its properties together with archival IFU and ALMA data. The deep NIRSpec spectrum reveals a broad H$β$ line with a width of $\sim1100$ km s$^{-1}$. We interpret it as a broad-line AGN whose line diagnostics are consistent with AGN activity across its clumpy structure, given the absence of little red dot signatures. MACS0416-Y1 clearly shows [OIII]4363 emission, suggesting a moderately low metallicity of $12+\log(\mathrm{O/H})=7.86^{+0.09}_{-0.08}$ ($0.15~Z_\odot$). The combination of [CII]158$μ$m and dust continuum emission indicates low dust mass ratios of $\log (M_{\rm dust}/M_{\rm gas})=-3.60^{+0.29}_{-0.22}$ and $\log (M_{\rm dust}/M_{\rm metal})=-0.95^{+0.29}_{-0.20}$. Because the metallicity of MACS0416-Y1 is around the critical metallicity of $0.1\textrm{-}0.2~Z_\odot$, the system is expected to undergo dust growth, explaining these low dust mass ratios as well as its small dust mass, $M_{\rm dust}\sim10^6~M_\odot$. The intense UV radiation from the AGN may contribute to a high dust temperature of $T_{\rm dust}\simeq 91^{+62}_{-35}$ K, boosting the dust-continuum emission above the ALMA detection limit despite the small $M_{\rm dust}$ at $z>8$. We find a very high total flux ratio of [OIII]88$μ$m/[OIII]5007 = $0.26 \pm 0.06$ in MACS0416-Y1, above predictions from single ionized nebular models at any electron density. This discrepancy suggests that the [OIII]88$μ$m and [OIII]5007 trace largely distinct regions, with the optical line suppressed in dusty nebulae, and thus requires careful interpretation when combining optical and infrared emission lines in JWST+ALMA studies.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a deep JWST/NIRSpec MSA spectrum of MACS0416-Y1 (z=8.312), revealing a broad Hβ line (~1100 km/s) indicative of an AGN, low metallicity (0.15 Z⊙), low dust/gas and dust/metal mass ratios, a high dust temperature (~91 K), and an anomalously high [OIII]88μm/[OIII]5007 flux ratio that suggests the two lines trace distinct nebular regions.
AI.motivation: To characterize the physical properties (AGN activity, metallicity, dust content, and emission-line diagnostics) of MACS0416-Y1, the highest-redshift galaxy with an ALMA dust continuum detection, by combining deep JWST/NIRSpec, IFU, and ALMA data.
AI.method: Deep JWST/NIRSpec MSA medium-grating spectroscopy combined with archival IFU and ALMA data; analysis of broad Hβ line, [OIII]4363 auroral line, [CII]158μm and dust continuum, and optical-to-infrared line ratios.
AI.result: Broad Hβ (~1100 km/s) indicates an AGN; low metallicity (12+log(O/H)=7.86, ~0.15 Z⊙); low dust-to-gas ratio (log(M_dust/M_gas)=-3.60) and low dust-to-metal ratio (log(M_dust/M_metal)=-0.95); high dust temperature (91 K) with small dust mass (~10^6 M⊙); very high [OIII]88μm/[OIII]5007 ratio (0.26±0.06) exceeding model predictions.
AI.conclusion: MACS0416-Y1 hosts an AGN at z>8 with low metallicity near the critical value for dust growth, explaining its low dust mass ratios. The high [OIII]88μm/[OIII]5007 ratio indicates that optical and infrared lines trace different ionized regions, requiring caution when combining JWST and ALMA emission-line data.

title: Probing the IMF in the Early Universe -- Direct measurements in the Boötes I UFD with JWST/NIRCam
comment: 26 pages, 15 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary: The dependence of the stellar initial mass function (IMF) on star-formation environment, particularly at low metallicities and high redshifts, remains poorly constrained. Ultra-faint dwarf galaxies (UFDs) are local fossils of high-redshift galaxies hosting old, metal-poor populations, and their resolved stellar populations provide unique pathways to constrain the sub-solar IMF. We investigate the low-mass IMF in the Boötes I (Boo I) UFD with JWST/NIRCam, leveraging its capability to resolve over 10,000 stars reaching $\lesssim0.15 M_{\odot}$, obtaining one of the largest, deepest resolved stellar samples for UFDs.
